headline: Mencast used AI to explore thousands of propulsion designs, and generated S$900,000 in new revenue.

metrics.label: Design turnaround
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

metrics.label: Productivity on knowledge-intensive tasks
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

metrics.label: New revenue
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

scqa.s: Mencast Marine provides marine propulsion design, manufacturing and repair for the global marine and offshore industry. Its design work draws on decades of engineering and sea-trial data. The company competes in a market where lower-cost suppliers can replicate standard designs, so differentiation has to come from engineering judgement applied to a specific vessel.
scqa.c: Conventional design methods restricted the number of options engineers could evaluate, which slowed complex projects. Competition from lower-cost players compressed margins and put pressure on a design-led business. Production cycles were long, and manual information retrieval slowed quotations, claims processing and research. The constraint was not engineering capability. It was the number of design options a small team could explore, and the time spent finding information that already existed inside the company. Quotation delays cost orders in a market where the buyer is comparing several suppliers on response time.
scqa.q: How could a mid-sized propulsion designer evaluate far more design options per project and speed up quotation work, without hiring a larger engineering team?
scqa.a: Mencast built the Mencast AI Platform, MAIP, which combines AI, computer vision and enterprise knowledge automation. AI-powered propulsion design analyses thousands of design possibilities to identify higher-performing options and shortens the design process. Design differentiation uses decades of engineering and sea-trial data, so the firm can offer solutions beyond price competition. Intelligent manufacturing optimisation combines AI, computer vision and sensors to improve quality and support more efficient production. Enterprise knowledge automation organises company knowledge and automates workflows including quotations, claims processing, research and information retrieval. The published result is 50% faster design turnaround, 75% higher productivity on knowledge-intensive tasks, and $900,000 in new revenue within 18 months. The revenue figure matters more than the efficiency figures, because it shows the capability was sold, not only used internally. The citation does not state how design options are validated, so it is not clear whether the model replaces simulation or only ranks candidates for it. The revenue figure is the strongest evidence in the citation, because it is the only one that shows an external buyer paying for the capability, rather than the company measuring its own internal efficiency.

takeaway: Point AI at the work you already charge for. Design exploration and quotation speed convert directly into won contracts.

headline: Oceanus Media Global films against AI-built virtual sets, cutting production timelines by around 80%.

metrics.label: Production timelines
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

metrics.label: Production costs
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

metrics.label: Multi-location project capacity
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

scqa.s: Oceanus Media Global is a creative media technology company specialising in virtual production, generative AI, content production, distribution and IP licensing. Third-party coverage from 2023 describes its work in virtual and augmented production. The company's cost base is driven by where it films, not only by what it films.
scqa.c: Multi-location productions could take 14 to 15 weeks, because location scouting, permits, travel, set construction and filming run in sequence. Location fees, permits, travel, transport and set construction added significant cost. Crews and equipment were largely committed to one major production at a time, which capped the number of concurrent projects. The business was therefore limited by logistics rather than by creative capacity. Each location added a fixed cost that had to be recovered whether or not the shoot ran to schedule.
scqa.q: How could the company produce multi-location content without moving a crew to each location, and take on more projects with the same crew?
scqa.a: Oceanus built an AI-integrated virtual production pipeline that creates multiple locations virtually. It combines generative AI, computer vision and AI agents across pre-production, filming, post-production and localisation, with creative control retained by the team. Pre-production support covers script breakdown, scene planning, scheduling, storyboarding and visualisation. AI-generated virtual environments create digital sets and reconstruct real locations for filming in a controlled studio. Actors are filmed against those environments with real-time camera tracking maintaining correct perspective. AI-supported visual effects automate repetitive editing tasks and help build effects elements. Localisation supports dubbing in four languages and adapts approved content for different formats and platforms. The published result is around 80% shorter production timelines, up to 85% lower production costs, and a 200% increase in multi-location project capacity. The economics change because the studio becomes the location. The citation does not name the generation models or describe the studio hardware, so the technical basis of the 80% figure is not documented. A cost reduction of this size changes which briefs are viable, not only how profitably existing ones are delivered, because a client with a modest budget can now be offered a multi-location treatment that was previously out of reach.

takeaway: Move the location into the studio, not the crew to the location. Fixed costs become reusable assets.

claims.text: Multi-location productions could take 14 to 15 weeks.
Actors are filmed against AI-built virtual environments with real-time camera tracking.
The pipeline supports dubbing in four languages and multi-format versioning.
Oceanus Media Global works in virtual and immersive production.

headline: ONG&ONG put 12,000 projects behind a search box and recovered 22,500 professional hours a year.

metrics.label: Workflow duration
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

metrics.label: Professional hours
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

metrics.label: Return on AI investment
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

scqa.s: ONG&ONG Group provides built environment consultancy across Asia, integrating architecture, urban master planning, landscape design, interior design and project management with civil, structural, mechanical and electrical engineering. The firm describes its offer as a 360 solution, which means a single project draws on several disciplines and decades of accumulated precedent.
scqa.c: The citation reports that up to 2,750 manhours a week went into searching for project precedents, building regulations, policies and project information scattered across multiple systems. Technical expertise sat with experienced staff, and retrieving knowledge from past projects required knowing the exact reference to search for. Regulatory, design, presentation and financial reporting tasks were manual. The knowledge existed, but access depended on knowing who held it and what it was called. New staff took longer to become useful, and senior staff became a lookup service for their own archive.
scqa.q: How could the firm make twelve thousand past projects and Singapore's building regulations searchable in plain language, so that any staff member could find precedent without asking a senior colleague?
scqa.a: ONG&ONG built 360i, an AI platform that connects project knowledge, regulatory information and business workflows in a governed environment. Knowledge retrieval lets staff search over 12,000 historical projects and internal information using plain-language questions, with answers linked back to source records. Dedicated assistants answer questions on Singapore building regulations and CORENET X requirements, with citations to the relevant clauses. Design visualisation generates and edits architectural, interior, urban and landscape concept images, so designers can explore several directions within hours. Financial reporting consolidates and validates data across 10 entities to produce the group profit and loss statement, with AI analyst modules generating alerts, forecasts and scenario analyses. The platform extends into PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook and document workflows. The published result is up to 95% savings in workflow duration, an estimated 22,500 professional hours recovered annually, and approximately 4x return on the AI investment. The citation-linked answer is the control that makes the system usable in a regulated profession. The citation does not report retrieval accuracy or the proportion of answers that staff accepted without checking the source. The return figure is approximate, but the hours figure is the one a practice can test against its own timesheets before committing, which makes it the more useful number for another firm deciding whether to build the same thing.

takeaway: Citation-linked retrieval is the difference between a search tool and a professional instrument. Architects can defend an answer they can source.

Staff search over 12,000 historical projects with answers linked to source records.

ONG&ONG operates a cross-discipline 360 solution across architecture, engineering and design.

headline: Supreme Components turned unstructured RFQs into structured data, cutting quote preparation time by up to 90%.

metrics.label: Sourcing and quote preparation
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

metrics.label: Bills of materials preparation
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

metrics.label: Productivity gains
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

scqa.s: Supreme Components International supplies active, passive and electromechanical components to original equipment manufacturers and electronics manufacturing companies. A distributor at this layer carries a wide franchise portfolio and competes on response speed and quoting accuracy. The work begins when a customer sends a request for quotation, often as an email with an attached spreadsheet or a PDF.
scqa.c: RFQs arrived in multiple formats and growing volumes, which made them difficult to process, track and manage. Manual product and brand matching increased the risk of quoting errors and caused avoidable follow-up. Supplier pricing and lead-time information was scattered across emails and records. Every quote therefore depended on a person assembling information from several places, and an error in part matching could produce a wrong price or a wrong lead time. Each avoidable follow-up consumed sales time twice: once to send the quote and again to correct it.
scqa.q: How could the distributor convert incoming RFQs of any format into structured, searchable requests and quote accurately without a person rebuilding the same information for every enquiry?
scqa.a: Supreme Components built Atlas, an AI RFQ-to-fulfilment platform. It extracts customer and product requirements from emails, PDFs, spreadsheets and other formats into structured data. Intelligent product matching matches requested products and brands against supplier information to streamline sourcing and quotation. Supplier intelligence extracts prices, inventory and lead times from emails, and identifies stock availability, supplier options and product alternatives. An automated workflow centralises RFQ and supplier information and automates supplier outreach, so information is easier to search, track and reuse. The published result is sourcing and quote preparation up to 90% faster, a 96% reduction in bills-of-materials preparation time, and up to $32,000 in monthly productivity gains. The durable asset is the structured record, because it makes the next similar RFQ cheaper than the last. The citation does not report line-item matching accuracy, which is the measure that determines whether the approach is safe at higher volumes. Bills-of-materials preparation is the sharper figure, because it measures a bounded task with a clear before and after, whereas sourcing time blends several activities that a distributor may define differently. Only then does the time saving translate into margin rather than into spare capacity.

takeaway: Extraction is only the first step. The value compounds when each parsed RFQ becomes reusable structured supply data.

Atlas extracts requirements from emails, PDFs and spreadsheets into structured data.
Supplier prices, inventory and lead times are extracted from emails.

headline: Thriving Weeds replaced 12-hour manual waste audits with continuous AI monitoring at over 95% accuracy.

metrics.label: Flagged contamination incidents
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

metrics.label: Waste weight data accuracy
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

metrics.label: Manhours per audit
metrics.attribution: Company-reported; published in the IMDA/SBF award citation

scqa.s: Thriving Weeds provides waste audits, data analysis and sustainability consultancy. Its clients need evidence of what they throw away, in what quantity, and how contaminated the waste streams are. That evidence usually underpins sustainability reporting and waste-reduction programmes. The company's own site describes AI- and IoT-enabled tracking for food waste segregation across multiple locations.
scqa.c: Conventional audits could involve six to eight people collecting and sorting waste for up to 12 hours a day. Short manual sampling periods made it hard to identify daily variation, repeated contamination or longer-term patterns. Repeated on-site audits and lengthy reporting required significant time for each premises. The result was a snapshot presented as a baseline, with the labour cost of producing it repeated for every site. Clients received a defensible snapshot, but not a trend, and the cost of the next snapshot was the same as the first.
scqa.q: How could the company measure waste continuously rather than in one exhausting sampling day, and do so across many premises without proportional labour?
scqa.a: Thriving Weeds built AuditEye, a waste-to-cloud ecosystem combining AI, IoT and cloud technology. Continuous monitoring captures disposal records throughout the deployment period, producing a larger and more representative dataset. AI-enabled contaminant detection identifies contaminants in waste streams and records when contamination occurs, including disposal weight and frequency. Automated data capture links images with weight, time, location and waste-stream information to create standardised records. Cloud processing handles records in near real time and provides access to waste data, images and downloadable records. Human-validated analysis combines continuous monitoring with consultant review and physical audits. The published result is 60% fewer flagged contamination incidents, more than 95% accuracy in waste weight measurement, and up to 384 manhours saved per audit. The company retains human verification and professional consultancy for recommendations, which keeps the output defensible. The citation does not describe the hardware or the reference method used to establish the 95% accuracy figure. The contamination figure is the commercial one, because clients buy a reduction in incidents rather than the accuracy of the measurement behind it, though the accuracy figure is what makes the incident count defensible in a report.

takeaway: Continuous measurement beats a heroic sampling day. A longer, lighter dataset is both cheaper and more credible.
